assessment.headline: DAY 34. Most volatile day of the war. RBI saved markets. But Trump won't secure Hormuz. India is on its own.
assessment.body:
Today was the most volatile day in Indian market history during this war. Sensex crashed 1,584 points at open after Trump's 'stone ages' speech, hit 71,551 intraday, then clawed back to close +185 at 73,320. The recovery was driven by RBI barring NDF contracts — rupee recovered to 93.19 from 94.84 ATL.

But the structural picture is deteriorating:
• Trump explicitly said the US will NOT secure Hormuz — 'countries must grab it and cherish it'
• Oil ROSE 5-7% after his speech, not fell. Markets read: more war = more disruption
• FII sold ₹8,331 Cr on Apr 1 alone. March total: ₹1.23 TRILLION
• India's manufacturing PMI hit a 4-year low
• IndiGo announced fuel surcharges ₹275-₹10,000 per ticket
• Gold crashed 4%, silver crashed 7%

India's fuel position remains managed short-term:
• 60 days stock (PIB confirmed). LPG 30+ days
• 800 TMT cargoes secured. Refineries >100%. 41+ suppliers
• ZERO dry-outs. 8 Hormuz carriers crossed. 18+485 remain
• Rupee recovered to 93.19 (from 94.84) on RBI intervention

But the long-term is alarming:
• Iran parliament approved permanent Hormuz tolls
• Trump won't secure the strait. India/Japan/Korea on their own
• Manufacturing PMI 4-year low signals economic slowdown starting
• The Week called it: 'Indian investors are falling for Trump's mood swings — the market is a sine wave'

Good Friday tomorrow — markets closed. 3-day weekend. April 6 deadline = 4 days. When markets reopen Monday, either talks have progressed or Trump's 'extremely hard' 2-3 weeks begins in earnest. India enters FY27 in the middle of the worst energy crisis since independence.
